WHY_THIS_LOT_AND_WHY_THIS_ACTOR.necessity_established_by_completed_readi: A discovery-ledger entry, DL-MECH-012, is tagged 'DATO (convergente su ≥3 modelli)' and describes WWOX loss as de-repressing inflammatory signalling across three models. Two of those three legs have now been read in this batch, and a proposal is already pending to keep the entry's DIRECTION while retiring the COUNT as a strength argument. The third leg is the lung and endothelial work, and nobody has read it. A convergence argument whose third leg is unread is an argument about a paper, not about evidence.
WHY_THIS_LOT_AND_WHY_THIS_ACTOR.second_reason_from_a_different_reading: The completed reading of PMID 16941225 found NO detectable WWOX in human endothelium by immunohistochemistry, while the endothelial leg of this axis rests on PMID 38563965. That reading recorded the discrepancy as a TENSION and explicitly not a refutation, which is the correct disposition and also precisely why the leg must be read rather than argued about. 🔴 Do not treat that tension as a conclusion: an adult-human IHC negative and a mouse or cell-culture knockdown model are different systems, and either could be right.
WHY_THIS_LOT_AND_WHY_THIS_ACTOR.why_scientist_c: Two reasons, and neither is slot-filling. First, inflammatory signalling sits inside this actor's contract theme. Second, and decisive: the pending proposal to retire the convergence count was authored by scientist-a, so the third leg must be read by an actor with NO stake in that proposal. This actor has none.

SCIENTIFIC_QUESTIONS.33058734: What does this study establish about WWOX and lung injury — which exposures, which model, which endpoints, which comparators, what n — and what does it NOT establish? Specifically: is the reported WWOX downregulation measured as transcript, as protein, or both; is the association with injury severity a measured effect of WWOX loss or a correlation between two consequences of the same exposure; and does the endothelial-specific knockout arm establish a cell-autonomous role or a tissue-level one?
SCIENTIFIC_QUESTIONS.38563965: What does the endothelial knockdown study add that the earlier paper does not already contain, and what does it NOT establish? In particular: is the inflammatory increase a cytokine measurement, a signalling readout or a transcriptome enrichment; is zyxin's role in it demonstrated by intervention or by correlation; and what, if anything, is shown about barrier function as opposed to inflammatory output?
SCIENTIFIC_QUESTIONS.joint_after_both: Does the pair establish that WWOX loss de-represses inflammatory signalling in this tissue, or does it establish something narrower — and is the second paper independent evidence or the same laboratory's next experiment on shared material? Answer from the artefacts, after both receipts exist.
SCIENTIFIC_QUESTIONS.the_axis_question_the_batch_needs: Whatever the pair establishes for LUNG and ENDOTHELIUM, state explicitly and separately what transfers toward a neurological reference genotype and what does not. A tissue-level inflammatory mechanism in lung is not a CNS mechanism, and saying so precisely is part of the deliverable rather than a hedge.

INTERNAL_EDGES.known_from_metadata: Both papers come from the Singla group with Aldaz as a middle author — 8th of 13 on 33058734 and 9th of 11 on 38563965 — so Aldaz is a collaborator here and not the senior author. Europe PMC carries a 'Preprint in' link for both records.
INTERNAL_EDGES.what_you_must_verify_rather_than_assume: 🔴 Same group and same disease model do NOT by themselves make the two papers dependent evidence. Establish from the artefacts whether the second reuses the first's animals, cell isolates, datasets or experiments; distinguish independence OF THE DATA from replication PERFORMED BY AN EXTERNAL GROUP; and do not report the pair as mutual confirmation unless the artefacts support it. Equally: do not infer dependence from an author list.

WAVE_3_RESULT.headline: The lot's two papers disagree about the axis's central claim, and the variable is not tissue but STIMULUS. PMID 33058734 measured lung inflammatory cytokines twice - LPS and MRSA - and found no significant difference either time, with both figure legends stating the null in their titles and no asterisk on any of six bars per figure at 600 dpi; its authors conclude an inflammation-INDEPENDENT mechanism. PMID 38563965, same laboratory and same knockout in the same tissue, measured them under MECHANICAL injury at n=10 and found IL-6, KC, IL-1beta and MCP-1 all significantly raised. DL-MECH-012 lists three legs and PMID 33058734 is not among them, so the entry's 'direzione univoca' is univocal only because the leg with the negative result is unlisted.
WAVE_3_RESULT.revival_trigger_answered: DL-MECH-012's own REVIVAL_TRIGGER asked for the system, species and whether PMID 38563965 shows basal endothelial WWOX by any method. Answered: human pulmonary ARTERY ECs in culture plus mouse lung ECs and whole-animal VILI; human and mouse; and YES - basal endothelial WWOX is detectable by two independent methods in the control condition (Fig 1A blot, Fig 1B immunostain), plus WWOX bands in mouse lung in Suppl Fig S1. The PREMISE: DEFAULT_FROM_TEXTBOOK dissolves. The findings are COMPATIBLE, not reconciled: the IHC negative is capillary and FFPE in situ, the positive is pulmonary artery in culture, and whether human capillary endothelium in situ expresses WWOX is left OPEN.
WAVE_3_RESULT.data_independence_verdict: The DATA are independent; the MATERIAL, the strain and the laboratory are shared; it is NOT replication by an external group. Shared: Aldaz's floxed allele, the strain (paper 2 says it was 'previously validated by our group (3)', and reference 3 IS paper 1), the senior laboratory and 8 authors. Not shared: different animals (n=3/arm at 18h vs n=10/group at 4h), different stimulus (LPS/MRSA vs VILI and cyclic stretch), different human cell type (lung MICROVASCULAR vs pulmonary ARTERY ECs), different endpoints (ECIS/transwell barrier vs proteomics/MAPK/cytokines - paper 2 contains no barrier assay at all), no shared dataset or cohort. So same-group-same-model did NOT make them dependent - and neither do they corroborate each other on inflammation, because where their questions touch they point opposite ways.
WAVE_3_RESULT.transfer_verdict: Stated separately from the tissue-level finding, as the contract requires: essentially NOTHING mechanistic transfers to a neurological reference genotype. Tissue is pulmonary microvascular and arterial endothelium with no BBB, astrocyte, pericyte or neuron measured anywhere; the positive inflammatory result requires ventilator-level mechanical stretch, which has no physiological analogue in the brain; the model is an adult tamoxifen-induced ~85% knockdown, not germline biallelic loss from conception, with all readouts acute at 4-18 h. The pair does NOT license a neuroinflammatory arm for a WWOX model: one half is a null and the other is mechanical, so using either as CNS support would be using it backwards. What has any claim to travel is gene-level and untested here: SOD2 (log2FC -0.94, the LARGER proteomic effect and the one the paper does not pursue) and the WWOX-SMAD3 link - both ESPANSIONE. One caution does transfer: p38 FALLS while ERK and JNK rise, so any model treating 'WWOX loss -> MAPK activation' as one direction is wrong in this tissue. And one method transfers: paper 1 shows inflammation and barrier failure can DISSOCIATE when both are measured in the same animals.

DEFAULTS_TAKEN.condition: The standing brief orders M4 receipt before M5 dossier, but a receipt's `outputs` must name only files that exist or session_self_eval raises UNRESOLVED_OUTPUT_FILE.
DEFAULTS_TAKEN.default: Wrote each dossier BEFORE recording that paper's receipt, so `outputs` named existing files.

DEFAULTS_TAKEN.what_would_have_been_different: A guessed PMID would have entered durable state looking exactly like a measured one.
